# Review context, round 2: remove thread-pool starvation observation

Range: 3e04f590 .. 2684bd14 (two follow-up commits on top of `feat!: remove thread-pool starvation
observation`, which removed `ParRuntime.openThreadPoolStarvationObservation(Duration)`,
`ThreadPoolStarvationObservationScope`, `ThreadPoolStarvationReport`, and
`ParRuntimeSnapshot.activeObservations()`).

Settled round-1 findings (confirmed and fixed in this range; do not re-raise unless the fix is wrong):

- `design/task-group-adopted-futures.md` header listed the removed observation.
- `README.md` / `README.zh-CN.md` capability claims listed starvation diagnostics.
- `BACKLOG.md` identity-probe entry cited the removed `NO_ISSUE` status.

Commits in range:

- `docs: drop stale starvation-observation references found in review` (the three fixes above).
- `test: pin timeout-action thread retirement at quiescence`: adds
  `ParRuntimeTest.quiescenceRetiresTheTimeoutActionThreads`, written after focused PIT showed that
  deleting `timeoutActionPool.shutdown()` in `ParRuntime.shutdownServicesWhenAdmissionsComplete`
  survived.

Read every changed file in the range. Attack surfaces: whether each documentation fix is accurate
against the code and the remaining contracts; whether the new test is deterministic, bounded, releases
what it creates, and actually detects the missing pool shutdown (and only that) through documented
behavior (`awaitQuiescence` and `releases()` Javadoc); Java 8/11 test-source compatibility; and any
stale reference to the removed API the first round missed anywhere in the repository's live documents.

Do not edit files.

summary: Reviewed the two follow-up commits (three documentation fixes and the new ParRuntimeTest.quiescenceRetiresTheTimeoutActionThreads test). The documentation fixes to README.md, README.zh-CN.md, BACKLOG.md, and the adopted-futures contract header are accurate against the current executor wait graph and ExecutorIdentity reference-equality contract, and the new test is deterministic, bounded, closes its runtime, and kills the deleted timeoutActionPool.shutdown() mutation through the documented awaitQuiescence()/releases() behavior. One stale starvation-observation reference remains in an Accepted ADR that the first-round documentation fix did not rewrite.

findings.title: Accepted ADR still lists the removed starvation observation as a live reconsideration signal
findings.trigger: A maintainer reads the Accepted ADR's 'Reconsider When' section to decide whether the TaskType removal should be revisited; the condition requires blocking-in-compute-pool incidents that the executor wait graph, starvation observation, application types, and blocking-call detectors all miss.
findings.consequence: The live ADR's reconsideration condition names a feature deleted in 0.5.0, so the condition cannot be evaluated as written and the document contradicts the removal note it carries in the same file.
findings.evidence: adr/0016-remove-tasktype-and-workload-fit-screening.md:110-111 still lists 'starvation observation' beside the executor wait graph; the 2026-11-27 note at lines 101-102 states that starvation observation was later removed and only the executor wait graph remains.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove 'starvation observation' from the Reconsider When bullet, and rewrite the costs bullet at lines 98-102 to state the post-removal signal set directly instead of relying on a parenthetical note.
